doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Fraternity record collection and pop music of the day
summary: He educated his Psi U brothers with LPs of Armstrong's Hot Fives and Sevens, and recalls Sinatra and Vaughn Monroe as pop.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Your frat brothers would have been listening to what else?
Well I educated many of them. My frat — we were all in Psi U House. And I was the one with the jazz collection.
Okay. But what did that have — or didn’t they have anything in particular? Did they have — you know what I think my question is —
Well actually you know the LP came out at that time. And we had George Avakian’s, Louis Armstrong’s Hot Five, Hot Sevens, on the Columbia green label.
Okay. The non-jazz music that they might have been listening to was what?

I don’t know. I just remember when I first started walking around New York by myself, before I even went to high school, I came in the summer, “I’m looking Over a Four Leaf Clover” was coming out of every little storefront. That was the thing. And of course well I mean Frank Sinatra, you know, a lot of people think he’s a jazz singer, I think he’s a © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
very good singer but I don’t really put him as a jazz singer. But that may be just my particular taste. And there was Vaughn Monroe. I mean all of those people were the pop people, yeah.
